Mathematical verdict for the scoped continuous-endpoint theorem: PASS under the ordinary premises below. All33 bound mathematical bodies were displayed whole and assessed. Essential source applications PASS; exhaustive source-label accuracy FAILS narrowly as n2 explains. Universal historical assertions remain INCONCLUSIVE as n3 explains. The exact domain is finite distinct complete rational equal-dimensional affine pages, pairwise intersection exactly one rational affine H of dimension less than d, arbitrary positive real page weights, and an actual continuous real PA PC reference γ on finite rational spatial geometry with strictly positive recession. There is no independence of quotient normal spaces. Every continuous printed-PC f with |f−γ| globally bounded has genuine finite rational-spatial real PA PC approximants strictly decreasing globally and converging uniformly, with the same actual page recession and a common relative bound. Several different overlaps, nonincident pages, general singular/glued/abstract categories and literal classification are excluded.

Ordinary premises are real completeness, finite-dimensional linear algebra and Gaussian elimination, Euclidean inner products, compactness of closed bounded sets/finite products, polynomial uniqueness and elementary convex secants; for the lattice steps, the Euclidean algorithm and saturated-subgroup extension to a lattice basis. The additional convex/polyhedral foundations are reconstructed as follows. For any real feasible point in a rational polyhedron, impose its active inequalities as equalities. A consistent rational system has a rational particular solution and rational kernel basis; rational coordinate approximation preserves the finitely many inactive positive slacks. This gives density in the minimal face. For a real PCC discard zero weights and use (α_j,t_j=α_jx_j), with α_j≥0, Σα_j=1, A_jt_j≥b_jα_j and Σt_j∈τ. These are rational linear constraints. Rational feasible approximants eventually retain positive weights; endpoints t_j/α_j and centers are rational and have the same face incidences. Continuity passes Jensen to every real-endpoint legal PCC, including irrational centers, without carrier coarsening.

Each inherited convex cell is contained in a page: a finite union of proper affine subspaces cannot cover its relative interior, by multiplying their nonzero affine equations and polynomial uniqueness. At a page point x, finitely many nonincident closed cells can be avoided by a neighborhood. Nearby x±u belong to incident cells. Rational density in z∈τ, z±v∈σ±, z,v∈L_i yields the local midpoint inequality. Subtract the chord on any real segment, obtaining q with zero endpoints. If q is positive inside, choose ε>0 small enough that q+εt² has an interior maximum. Its sufficiently nearby symmetric average is at least its center value plus εs², contradicting the local midpoint inequality and maximality. Thus each full page is convex; no uniform radius is assumed.

Finite full-domain convex functions are locally Lipschitz: cube vertex values give an upper bound, reflection gives a lower bound on a smaller cube, and extending secants a fixed distance bounds both difference quotients. Directional derivatives are finite continuous sublinear by secant monotonicity, Lipschitz estimates, rescaling and the convex inequality at 2tv,2tw. Nearest-point separation of z outside a closed convex C gives n=w−z with n·(c−z)≥|n|²>0. Apply this below a continuous full-domain epigraph and take limiting inward unit normals. The vertical coefficient is nonnegative and cannot be zero, since full spatial projection would then force the spatial coefficient zero too. Division gives touching affine supports and full-domain biconjugacy. A touching support ℓ+b of a sublinear derivative at w has b≤0 by testing zero and b≥0 by testing 2w. Thus b=0. Forms below the derivative are exactly page subgradients; the two-sided norm bound makes their defining closed convex sets nonempty compact, with h_i(w)=max_{K_i}ℓ(w).

At any real y∈H let K=∏K_i and S=image(E*→∏L_i*) for E=ΣL_i. S is the ENTIRE closed restriction image. If K misses S, minimize |pr_{S⊥}z|² on K. For a=pr_{S⊥}z_0≠0, differentiating segments gives a·z≥|a|². Represent −a by page vectors w_i. Orthogonality gives the actual ambient relation Σw_i=0 and product maximization gives Σh_i(w_i)≤−|a|²<0. For small t, the endpoints y+tw_i are in incident cells, have equal-weight center y and negative total cost. Perspective density makes this a legal real-endpoint PCC, contradicting PC. Hence one ambient form supports every page at y. Conversely a center outside H has all its incident endpoint cells in its unique page, so ordinary Jensen applies; at a center in H summing one common ambient support cancels its barycenter term. Matching traces alone is insufficient.

Finite hull/cone foundations require no unnamed theorem. An affine dependence among more than a+1 positive hull coefficients has zero sum and both signs. Subtract t times that dependence up to the first zero coefficient; iterate. Thus conv(K) is the image of K^{a+1} times a compact simplex and is compact. Conic dependence reduction leaves independent active columns, whose finitely many inverse maps bound coefficients; a convergent sequence has a convergent representation on one subset, so finite cones are closed. For cones given by finite inequalities remove their homogeneous kernel as lineality; the sum of nonnegative defining forms has a bounded section at one. Add both signs of a basis of the removed lineality; a zero quotient needs no section. On a bounded polyhedron, move in both directions in the kernel of active constraints until rank increases; boundedness supplies endpoints and induction terminates at finitely many vertices. Rational full-rank systems give rational vertices. Homogenization gives pointed polyhedron vertex-hull plus recession generation: positive-height extreme rays normalize to vertices, since a nontrivial affine decomposition would split the ray; zero-height rays are recession generators. The height equation makes the positive-height coefficients sum to one. Fourier–Motzkin pairing of lower/upper bounds and equality elimination gives finite inequality descriptions and projections.

A finite LSC convex a on a compact polytope is continuous on its WHOLE domain: vertex values bound it above by M. At x choose a fixed radius below every inactive slack/normal norm in its affine span. Every nearby feasible direction extends to that radius while retaining all active inequalities. Convexity gives a(z)≤(1−t)a(x)+tM, t→0; LSC gives the other inequality. For compact-domain extended biconjugacy, strictly separate (q,t), t<a(q), below the closed epigraph. Testing (q,a(q)) in the SAME fiber forces the vertical coefficient β strictly positive; division gives affine minorants approaching a(q), including boundary. Outside the compact domain a spatial separator u gives u(q)>max_Ku and (su)(q)−a*(su)→∞ because min_Ka is finite. Thus a=a** everywhere, including outside.

On one complete page, actual convex γ is the maximum of its finitely many affine top-cell supports. Set h=max actual gradients and Δ their hull. Constants bound γ−h. Carrier recession cones cover full space by taking an unbounded subsequence of tv in one cell and dividing its inequalities by t; h equals its cell slope there. Strict positive recession makes cells pointed and puts zero inside Δ. Rational spatial recession rays lifted with REAL heights h(r), plus the upward ray, generate exactly epi(h), since h is linear on each cone and sublinear globally. For |f−h| bounded, φ=f* is finite bounded exactly on Δ; outside, a spatial separating ray gives infinity. It is convex LSC, hence continuous on the whole polytope. Full-domain biconjugacy gives f=φ* and f(x+v)≤f(x)+h(v).

Choose rational samples whose affine dual values approximate φ within η on neighborhoods covering ALL compact Δ; append ANY finite rational contacts. Then φ−η≤g_A=max_a[p(a)−f(a)]≤φ. E_A=conv{(a,f(a))}+epi(h) is closed by compact-plus-closed-cone, has full projection and lies inside epi(f) by convexity/recession. Its vertical fibers attain finite lower F_A. Maximizing over generators gives F_A*=g_A on Δ and infinity outside; biconjugacy yields f≤F_A≤f+η globally and exact contacts. Lower facets have positive vertical coefficient because projection is full. Each lower graph face projects affinely bijectively to a hull of rational positions plus rational rays, regardless of real heights. Intersections are faces preserved by that affine bijection. These projections give a genuine finite rational carrier. Shared-face matching at rational affine basis points is a rational homogeneous coefficient system; its rational kernel basis and denominator clearing of tangent slopes prove genuine real scalar extension of literal PA without slope rounding or irrational-wall assertions.

For page conjugates φ_i define D={p:r_ip∈Δ_i all i}, φ=max_iφ_i(r_ip), T=p|H. D is a closed real polyhedron and bounded: an unbounded normalized sequence would limit to a unit covector annihilating all spanning pages. Common support gives nonemptiness and simultaneous Fenchel equality. Thus G=φ* satisfies G|L_i≤f_i and G|H=f_H, without extension equality elsewhere. The attained compact fiber minimum k(q)=min_{Tp=q}φ(p) is convex by mixing and LSC by subsequences. Its domain T(D) is a compact polytope; whole continuity and extended biconjugacy yield k*=f_H, k=f_H*, T(D)=Δ_H INCLUDING every boundary fiber. Separate page fiber minima k_i have the same conjugate f_H, hence equal k as extended functions. Every page value is at least k; at a joint max minimizer all are at most k and therefore ALL equal k simultaneously. M={p:φ(p)=k(Tp)} is compact and surjects onto all Δ_H.

For f_H≤g≤f_H+η, b=g* is continuous on the whole Δ_H with k−η≤b≤k. Define S_i={(r_ip,b(Tp)):p∈M}, E_i=conv(graph φ_i∪S_i)+vertical-up. Compact-hull elimination makes E_i closed with finite attained lower ψ_i on Δ_i. Sources and epigraph convexity give φ_i−η≤ψ_i≤φ_i and ψ_i≥b∘U_i. ONE joint p over each q gives ψ_i(r_ip)=b(q) for ALL pages, so every page fiber minimum equals b. F_i=ψ_i* is finite continuous convex, f_i≤F_i≤f_i+η globally, exact recession and whole trace g. At EVERY real y pick an attained trace q and ONE p∈M over q. Then F_i(x)≥p(x)−b(q)=g(y)+p(x−y) on all pages. These non-PA intermediate functions are not measured.

For finite rational-spatial real PA g, pointed-cell generation gives ENTIRE epi(g) as the hull of ALL rational vertex lifts plus exact epi(h_H). Apply the page primal construction to F_i, appending ALL those vertices and using the exact actual page cone. Its epigraph contains epi(g) over H, hence Q_i|H≤g; above F_i gives ≥g. Thus whole trace equality and all common supports survive, with global error≤2η. Rational ambient equations defining H, extended trace equations and page-wall equations give a finite arrangement refining all carriers and common faces on H; no coefficient equality creates irrational cuts. Take η_n=2^{-n}, n≥1, and P_n=Q_n+4η_n. Globally 4η_n≤P_n−f≤6η_n and P_{n+1}−f≤3η_n<4η_n≤P_n−f. This proves strict decrease/uniform convergence, exact recession and relative bound C+3. For H=0 append zero to each separate page sample set; exact center value preserves every original common support and the simpler error≤η_n. Shifted contacts need not remain exact.

R230 supplies continuity/PC and |P_γ(u)−γ|≤||u|| for every unrestricted u∈C_b on this positive balanced geometry; it supplies no PA density. The construction above then proves endpoint domain membership before completed MA. Upper-only competitors may be replaced by max(q,γ−||u||), which stays PC by active-center Jensen, remains below the obstacle and is bounded both ways; this is not irrational PA max closure.
